turns.teacher: Yes, tum travelled some distance going out and back. Even though you ended where you started, every step counts toward distance. Suppose tum dance 4 metres out and 4 metres back in 4 seconds. What is your average speed?

end.summary:
- Practised calculating speed from distance ÷ time; some calculations were correct.
- Practised average velocity as displacement ÷ time; return to the starting point was identified as zero displacement and zero average velocity.
- Practised distinguishing speed from velocity using path length and final position; this still needs checking next time.
- Practised that acceleration can involve a change in velocity; the idea that a change in direction causes acceleration was still mixed up at the last check.
end.parentNote: At home, ask Diya to list whether speed, direction, or both change in three examples, such as braking, turning, and moving straight at constant speed.
